coldRead: An AI agent (Claude Code or Codex) runs `crumb launch <id>`. The Crumb CLI spawns a detached supervisor (`__supervise`) and then polls the vault directory for a run handle file. The supervisor gets the vault key from the OS key store (Keychain or secret-tool, falling back to CRUMB_KEY or a key file) and decrypts the saved session. It injects the cookies and state into a local Chrome over CDP and autosaves every 30s, on SIGUSR2 and on SIGTERM, merging changes so concurrent runs don't overwrite each other. The agent then drives Chrome directly over CDP. A PreToolUse hook (Vault guard) blocks agent tool calls that touch ~/.crumb. If the key is missing, crumb fails closed instead of creating a new key. If startup takes longer than 60s, it reports the supervisor's .error file, or INTERNAL if there isn't one.
inaccuracies: The CLI→vault edge is labelled 'poll handle file', but nothing shows the CLI printing the handle/CDP endpoint back to the agent, which is how the agent reaches Chrome (src/session.ts, src/cli.ts).
The 'encrypted session' edge goes one way only (supervisor→vault), but the supervisor both loads and autosaves sessions (src/session.ts autosave around line 212).

The supervisor→keystore edge is drawn as a one-way sync lookup. src/crypto.ts also falls back to CRUMB_KEY or a key file and can store a newly created key (crypto.ts:84), so the store is not only read.
The legend line 'AI red; your additions blue' describes an authoring workflow, not the system, and the image contains no blue.
improvements: Add numbered steps and an explicit return edge (CLI → agent: 'prints CDP endpoint/handle'), so the order of the flow and how the agent finds Chrome can be read without a walkthrough.
Re-route 'CDP automation' so it doesn't run along the frame edge, keep labels off the lines, fix the wrapped ']' in the frame title, and use the empty margin to enlarge the body text for 1194x834.

Make the notation actually distinguishable: use clearly different line styles or a second color for sync vs local-IO edges, give the external OS key store its own visual treatment, drop the 'AI red/blue' text, and note what happens when Chrome or the supervisor crashes.
